verifications.claim: Artemis II is NASA’s 10-day crewed flight test.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "Scheduled for almost 10 days" (R1); "The approximately 10-day Artemis II mission" (R3); "Mission duration9 days, 1 hour, 32 minutes" planned as 10-day (R7); "The 10-day Artemis II mission" (R9)
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources directly describe Artemis II as an approximately 10-day crewed test flight.

verifications.claim: Artemis II is scheduled to launch no earlier than September 2025.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "the delay of Artemis II’s launch, which was previously scheduled for no earlier than September 2025."
verifications.reasoning: R1 directly states the schedule as no earlier than September 2025.

verifications.claim: Artemis II will send four astronauts around the Moon and back.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "send humans around the moon" (R1); "lifting four astronauts toward space... around the moon but not land there" (R2); "around the Moon and back to Earth" (R3); "journey around the Moon and back" (R5)
verifications.reasoning: All sources confirm four astronauts on a lunar flyby around the Moon and back.

verifications.claim: Artemis II marks the first human mission to lunar vicinity since 1972.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "first trip astronauts will take outside Earth orbit since 1972" (R1); "first crewed mission to the moon in more than 50 years" (R2); "first crewed flight beyond low Earth orbit since Apollo 17 in 1972" (R7)
verifications.reasoning: Sources explicitly state it as the first since 1972 (Apollo 17).

verifications.claim: Artemis II tests the Orion spacecraft.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "Artemis I tested... SLS and Orion... Artemis II is set to send humans around the moon" (R1); "test the capabilities of the Orion spacecraft" (R5); "test flight supporting subsequent Artemis missions" (R7)
verifications.reasoning: Directly described as a test of Orion.

verifications.claim: Artemis II tests the SLS rocket.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "Artemis I tested out the ground systems, rocket, and spacecraft... Artemis II" (R1); "SLS (Space Launch System) rocket, with the Orion spacecraft" (R3)
verifications.reasoning: Sources confirm SLS testing on Artemis II.

verifications.claim: Artemis II crew includes NASA astronaut Reid Wiseman.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "Commander Wiseman" (R1); "Reid Wiseman, the NASA astronaut who is the commander" (R2)
verifications.reasoning: All crew sources list Reid Wiseman as commander.

verifications.claim: Artemis II crew includes NASA astronaut Victor Glover.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "Pilot Victor Glover" (R1); "Victor Glover" (R2)
verifications.reasoning: Consistently listed as pilot.

verifications.claim: Artemis II crew includes NASA astronaut Christina Koch.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "Christina Koch" (R1); "Christina Koch" (R2)
verifications.reasoning: Consistently listed as mission specialist.

verifications.claim: Artemis II crew includes CSA astronaut Jeremy Hansen.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "Jeremy Hansen of the Canadian Space Agency" (R1); "CSA (Canadian Space Agency) astronaut Jeremy Hansen" (R3)
verifications.reasoning: Explicitly identified as CSA astronaut.

verifications.claim: Artemis II will fly approximately 4,700 miles (7,600 km) beyond the far side of the Moon.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "between 5,000 and 9,000 nautical miles beyond the far side" (R1, ~5,750-10,350 mi); "flying almost 7500 km beyond the Moon" (R5, ~4,660 mi)
verifications.reasoning: R5 closely matches 7,500 km ≈ 4,700 mi; R1 range includes approximate value.

verifications.claim: Artemis II surpasses previous crewed flight distances.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "This crew will travel farther than any humans ever have before" (R1); "set a distance record... 4,144 miles farther than the Apollo 13" (R2)
verifications.reasoning: Explicitly states surpassing previous records like Apollo 13.

verifications.claim: The primary goal of Artemis II is to demonstrate that Orion’s life-support systems can keep astronauts safe during a deep-space journey.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "test flights... testing and proving out the systems... life support" (R1); "flight test Orion’s life-support systems with astronauts on board" (R9)
verifications.reasoning: Directly supports life-support testing as key goal.

verifications.claim: Artemis II will make Victor Glover the first person of color to travel beyond low Earth orbit.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "Mr. Glover... will be the first Black man to venture into deep space" (R2); "Victor Glover (an African-American) became the first person of color" (R7)
verifications.reasoning: Directly stated.

verifications.claim: Artemis II will make Christina Koch the first woman to travel beyond low Earth orbit.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "Ms. Koch... will be the first woman to do so" (R2); "Christina Koch the first woman" (R7)
verifications.reasoning: Directly stated.

verifications.claim: Artemis II will make Jeremy Hansen the first non-U.S. citizen to travel beyond low Earth orbit.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "Mr. Hansen... will be the first person on a moon mission who is not an American" (R2); "Jeremy Hansen the first non-U.S. citizen" (R7)
verifications.reasoning: Directly stated.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II crew will manually pilot the Orion spacecraft in Earth's orbit to assess its handling.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "Mr. Glover manually flew the spacecraft" (R2); "manually maneuver Orion relative to another spacecraft" (R3); "take manual control of the spacecraft to conduct a proximity operations demonstration" (R5)
verifications.reasoning: Proximity operations demo involves manual piloting in Earth orbit.

verifications.claim: Artemis II will perform a scenic loop around the Moon.
verifications.label: VAGUE
verifications.evidence: "long slingshot around the moon"; "circling it in a figure eight on a free-return trajectory" (R1); "fly around our natural satellite" (R5)
verifications.reasoning: Describes loop around Moon, but 'scenic' is interpretive.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II crew will photograph terrain around the Moon that has not been closely examined in over 50 years.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "photograph... terrain... up to 60 percent of their far side view may be unique"; "having human eyes look at the moon up close could give us important scientific insights"
verifications.reasoning: Crew to photograph previously unseen lunar terrain.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II crew will study terrain around the Moon that has not been closely examined in over 50 years.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "observe the lunar surface... parts of the moon humans haven’t experienced before"; "lunar science lead... packing as much scientific observations"
verifications.reasoning: Crew observations and descriptions constitute study of unseen terrain.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II team will perform ongoing medical tests.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "We have three different experiments on board... blood draws and wet saliva samples pre- and post-mission... dry saliva samples... obstacle course"
verifications.reasoning: Multiple ongoing human health experiments described.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II team will monitor the crew’s health in deep space.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "Their bodies will also be put to the test... surveys... psychological well-being and sleep patterns... assess how space changes the astronauts’ physiology"
verifications.reasoning: Explicit health monitoring via experiments.

verifications.claim: Exploration Mission-2 (EM-2) is the original designation of Artemis II.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "Originally designated Exploration Mission-2 (EM-2)"
verifications.reasoning: Directly stated.

verifications.claim: Artemis II is commonly compared to 21st Century Apollo 8 due to similar orbit mission profile.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "the 21st century equivalent of Apollo 8" (R2); "objectives were similar to those of Apollo 8" (R7)
verifications.reasoning: Explicit comparison to Apollo 8.

verifications.claim: SLS (Space Launch System) is the 32-story rocket lifting the Artemis II crew.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "322-foot-tall rocket" (≈32 stories, 10 ft/story)
verifications.reasoning: Height matches 32-story approximation.

verifications.claim: Orion spacecraft is named Integrity.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "spacecraft named Integrity" (R2); "Orion spacecraft, named Integrity" (R3)
verifications.reasoning: Directly named.

verifications.claim: Orion spacecraft is designed to take humans deeper into space than ever before.
verifications.label: VAGUE
verifications.evidence: "Orion... will take astronauts into Earth orbit... to the moon... new era of human exploration of the cosmos"
verifications.reasoning: Designed for deep space/Moon/Mars, but not explicitly 'deeper than ever before'; mission does achieve it.

verifications.claim: European Service Module (ESM-2) powers the spacecraft.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "provides the Orion spacecraft... with... power" (R5); "solar array wings... giving Orion... power" (R3, ESM context)
verifications.reasoning: ESM provides power.

verifications.claim: European Service Module (ESM-2) propels the spacecraft.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "provides... propulsion" (R5); "ESM’s engines" (R5)
verifications.reasoning: ESM provides propulsion.

verifications.claim: European Service Module (ESM-2) sustains the spacecraft.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "provides... life support" (R5); "life support systems to keep the crew safe" (R5)
verifications.reasoning: ESM provides life support/sustenance.
